story.head: Somebody warn Yaroslav Askarov
paras: The Sharks (7-7-1) lost 5-1 to Ottawa on Saturday, while the Wild (10-3-3) beat Washington 5-1 on Sunday. Going in, the Sharks are fourth in the Pacific (tied for 19th in the NHL) and the Wild first in the Central (second).
The Sharks’ record (.500) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.367), largely thanks to their goaltending. The Wild’s record (.719) is about what their chances are worth.

The Sharks are one of the league’s most physical teams (2nd) and ice the puck a lot (32nd). They also do a lot of their shooting from distance (2nd lowest), so the Wild get in close, but them mostly shoot from distance. As for the Wild, they draw more penalties than they take (2nd) and leave the shooting to their forwards (3rd lowest), but get pinned in their own end on long shifts (31st). Minnesota has allowed 2.25 goals a game, the third fewest in the league. The Wild are likely to get plenty of pucks to the net against the Sharks.

Macklin Celebrini (5 G / 11 A / 16 P in 13 GP) leads the Sharks in scoring, with a point in six straight games against Minnesota. Will Smith (6 G / 4 A / 10 P in 15 GP) has a team-high six goals. Kirill Kaprizov (15 G / 10 A / 25 P in 16 GP) leads the Wild in scoring and is third in the NHL, with eight points in his last five games and seven goals in eight games against San Jose since 2023-24. Quinn Hughes (5 G / 16 A / 21 P in 16 GP) isn’t far behind, with eight points in his last five games.
Yaroslav Askarov (4-5-0 / .900 SV% in 9 GS) is in line to start for San Jose. Jesper Wallstedt (9-2-3 / .919 SV% in 14 GS) has been outstanding for Minnesota and will likely start.
The Wild usually control more of the chances than the Sharks do.

items.text: The Wild are newly without Jared Spurgeon, have been without Marcus Foligno since Oct 8, and have had to make do without Filip Gustavsson and Brock Faber all season. Jesper Wallstedt is expected to start.
The Sharks have been without Igor Chernyshov and Alexander Wennberg for several games.
Joel Eriksson Ek has four goals on chances worth about 9.0 goals, well below what his finishing usually turns chances into. If the chances keep coming, so should the goals.
Quinn Hughes, Kirill Kaprizov, Joel Eriksson Ek and Matt Boldy have a point in five straight games.
